learn.hook: Switch off the lights and look out of the window. What can you see and hear at night?
points: The lesson 'Night' is a poem about the quiet beauty of the night.
Poems sometimes talk about things as if they were people: 'The sun has gone to bed.'
Sound words help us hear the night: an owl's 'hoo', the crickets' song.
Rhyming words: last – past, bright – goodnight, tree – me.

example.q:
Read our poem:
The sun has gone to bed at last,
The day of play is done and past.
The moon peeps out, so round and bright,
The stars come out to wink goodnight.
An owl calls 'hoo' from the mango tree,
And sleepy crickets sing to me.
What does 'The sun has gone to bed' really mean?
steps: The sun cannot really sleep in a bed.
The poet means the sun cannot be seen any more.
This happens in the evening, when the sun sets.
example.answer: It means the sun has set and the night has begun.

learn.reallife: Look at the night sky from your terrace with an elder. You may hear crickets or see the moon peeping out from the clouds.

games.title: True or false? (about our poem)
items: In the poem, the moon is round and bright.
The poem says 'The moon peeps out, so round and bright.'
The owl calls from a neem tree.
The owl calls from the mango tree.
The stars 'wink goodnight' in the poem.
The fourth line says the stars come out to wink goodnight.
'last' and 'past' are rhyming words.
Both end with the '-ast' sound.
In the poem, the crickets are wide awake and loud.
The poem calls them 'sleepy crickets'.

games.title: Day or night?
items: the sun shines high in the sky
children go to school
a rainbow appears after rain
the rooster crows at dawn
stars twinkle in the sky
owls hunt for food
we sleep in our beds
fireflies glow

quiz.q: Read: 'The sun has gone to bed at last.' What does this line mean?
options: The sun is in a bed.
quiz.explain: The poet talks about the sun like a person. It means the sun has set.
quiz.mistake: Takes the line word for word

quiz.q: Read: 'The moon peeps out, so round and bright.' How does the moon look?
quiz.explain: The line says the moon is 'round and bright'.
quiz.mistake: Did not read the describing words in the line

quiz.q: Read: 'The stars come out to wink goodnight.' What do the stars do?
quiz.explain: The stars 'wink goodnight'. Twinkling stars look like they are winking.
quiz.mistake: Mixed up the stars with the crickets that sing

quiz.q: Read: 'An owl calls hoo from the mango tree.' Where is the owl?
quiz.explain: The line says the owl calls from the mango tree.
quiz.mistake: Did not read the line carefully

quiz.q: Read: 'And sleepy crickets sing to me.' Who sings in the poem?
quiz.explain: The line says the sleepy crickets sing.
quiz.mistake: Mixed up the owl's call with the crickets' song

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'bright'?
quiz.explain: 'bright' and 'goodnight' both end with the '-ight' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that only begins the same way

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'last'?
quiz.explain: 'last' and 'past' both end with the '-ast' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that begins with the same letter

quiz.q: Read: 'The moon peeps out.' What does 'peeps' mean here?
quiz.explain: To peep is to look out a little, quietly.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'peep'

teach.ask: Gappu is a little scared of the dark. He asks: 'What happens in the night poem?'
teach.praise: The night is not scary at all! The moon peeps and the stars wink. Goodnight!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what the moon, the stars and the owl do in the poem?

learn.hook: The moon shines so brightly at night. But did you know it has no light of its own?
points: The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight falls on it.
Stars make their own light. The Sun is a star. It is the star nearest to the Earth.
Stars look tiny because they are very, very far away.
The Moon seems to change its shape over about a month. On a full moon night (Purnima) we see the whole round Moon. On a new moon night (Amavasya) we cannot see it.
The Moon goes around the Earth.

example.q: Why can we not see the stars in the daytime, even though they are still in the sky?
steps: In the day, the Sun lights up the whole sky.
The sunlight is much brighter than the faraway stars.
So the bright sunlight hides them from our eyes.
example.answer: Because the bright sunlight hides the stars in the daytime.

learn.reallife: On a full moon night, look up: the whole round moon lights up your street!

games.title: Match the sky words
pairs: the whole round Moon is seen
what stars seem to do at night

games.title: True or false?
items: The Moon makes its own light.
The Moon shines because sunlight falls on it.
The Sun is a star.
The Sun is a star. It is the nearest star to the Earth.
Stars look small because they are very far away.
Stars are huge, but they are very, very far away.
On a new moon night, we see the whole round Moon.
We cannot see the Moon on a new moon night. We see the whole Moon on a full moon night.
The Moon goes around the Earth.
The Moon moves around the Earth.
Most owls are awake at night.
Most owls rest in the day and hunt at night.

quiz.q: Does the Moon make its own light?
options: No, it shines because sunlight falls on it.
Yes, it is a big lamp.
quiz.explain: The Moon has no light of its own. Sunlight falling on it makes it look bright.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Moon glows by itself like the Sun

quiz.q: Which of these is a star?
quiz.explain: The Sun is a star that makes its own light.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Moon is a star because it shines at night

quiz.q: Why do stars look so small?
options: because they are tiny like sand
because they are very, very far away
because they are made of paper
quiz.explain: Stars are huge, but they look tiny because they are so far away.
quiz.mistake: Thinks stars are really small

quiz.q: What do we call the night when we see the whole round Moon?
quiz.explain: On a full moon night (Purnima), the whole round Moon shines.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up full moon and new moon

quiz.q: What do we call the night when we cannot see the Moon at all?
quiz.explain: On a new moon night (Amavasya), the Moon cannot be seen.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up new moon and full moon

quiz.q: The Moon goes around the ___.
quiz.explain: The Moon goes around the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what the Moon goes around

quiz.q: Why can we not see stars in the daytime?
options: The stars go away in the day.
The stars sleep in the day.
The stars fall into the sea.
quiz.explain: The stars are still there, but sunlight is too bright for us to see them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the stars disappear in the day

quiz.q: Which of these is awake and hunts at night?
quiz.explain: Owls hunt at night. Cows, sparrows and butterflies rest at night.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which animals are active at night

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Does the moon have a big torch inside? Are stars tiny?'
teach.praise: No torch! The moon shines with sunlight, and stars are faraway suns. Wow!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me where the Moon gets its light and why stars look small?

learn.hook: Day and night are best friends who never meet. One comes and the other goes!
points: Opposites are words with completely different meanings.
day – night, dark – bright, sleep – wake, early – late.
rise – set, up – down, open – close, noisy – quiet.
Opposites help us compare and describe things clearly.

example.q: What is the opposite of 'rise' in this sentence? 'The sun rises in the morning.'
steps: The sun rises in the morning.
In the evening, it goes down.
The word for going down is 'sets'.
example.answer: set (The sun sets in the evening.)

learn.reallife: Your day is full of opposites: you wake up early, go out and come in, turn the lights on and off, and go to sleep at night.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'day'?
quiz.explain: Day and night are opposites.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that goes with day instead of its opposite

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'dark'?
quiz.explain: Dark and bright are opposites. Black, dim and shadowy go with dark.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with a similar meaning

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'sleep'?
quiz.explain: When you stop sleeping, you wake.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that is like sleeping

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'early'?
quiz.explain: Early and late are opposites.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the opposite of early

quiz.q: Fill in: 'The sun rises in the morning and ___ in the evening.'
quiz.explain: The opposite of rise is set.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the same word instead of its opposite

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'noisy'?
quiz.explain: Noisy and quiet are opposites. 'Loud' means almost the same as noisy.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with the same meaning

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'open'?
quiz.explain: Open and close are opposites.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that goes with open

quiz.q: Which pair of words are opposites?
quiz.explain: Up and down are opposites. The others mean the same.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up opposites with words that mean the same

teach.ask: Gappu says: 'The night is dark. What is the opposite of dark? What are opposites?'
teach.praise: Dark – bright, night – day! Opposites are fun!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what opposites are and give me two pairs?
